newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Hui Shung to crush soy in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Hui Shung to crush soy in Philippines.

text.p: Taiwan's Hui Shung Agriculture and Food Corp said on Wednesday its soybean crushing plant under construction in the Philippines could begin producing soy oil and soymeal in 1998.
"Our new plant can start running by early 1998 to provide soy oil and soymeal to the Philippine market," a Hui Shung official told Reuters by telephone.
The plant would have the capacity to crush up to 300,000 tonnes of soybeans a year, which would produce about 60,000 tonnes of soy oil and 240,000 tonnes of soymeal, he said.
Hui Shung invested over US$8 million to build the crushing plant north of Manila, the official said.

The Philippines, whose main grain crop is rice, opened an advanced grain terminal in June with capacity to handle two 54,000-tonne class Panamax-type bulk vessels simultaneously, enabling the country to expand its grains processing.
